Tagcast 0.30.0 adds reviewed batch metadata cleanup, full random album playback,
fullscreen Now playing and colour palettes. All features are included in the
standalone downloads for macOS, Windows and Linux.

## Reviewed metadata cleanup

- Open **Overview → Metadata health → Clean up metadata…** to split combined
  **genres, track artists or composers** across your active library. Only
  semicolons are split; slashes, commas and ampersands stay intact. Album artists
  and unrelated metadata remain unchanged.
- Preview the before/after values, exclude albums and export the report, then
  explicitly approve and start. Batches contain at most **200 tracks from
  20 displayed albums**. Each batch checks current values and reads accepted
  changes back before sending the next one.
- **Review genre labels** searches exact stored labels. Rename one label, replace
  it with multiple labels entered one per line, or explicitly remove it while
  preserving each track's other genres. A label such as `Films/Games` is never
  automatically split. Empty replacement text alone cannot delete a label.
- Progress distinguishes confirmed, outstanding and unconfirmed tracks. Conflicts,
  request errors or unconfirmed writes stop processing. Stop/resume and an
  account-scoped local report make long jobs reviewable; resume rechecks current
  values. There is no batch Undo.
- Additional performers now participate in Track artists browsing, search and
  track/player links, independently of composer credits.

## Album playback and appearance

- **Play random album** starts a complete album in track/disc order from your
  filtered collection, an album artist, genre, composer, track artist, year or
  decade. It chooses across all pages and the full matching decade, replaces
  the queue and avoids the current album when alternatives exist.
- **Fullscreen Now playing** focuses on the cover and track information, keeping
  the same audio element and controls. Escape returns to browsing. Browsers that
  cannot enter native fullscreen use a window-filling view.
- The **Theme** menu offers **Forest, Ocean, Warm and iBroadcast inspired** colours,
  independently of **Auto, Light and Dark** appearance. Preferences remain local
  to the browser; changing them keeps playback running.
- Album cards use a compact queue **+** and aligned information rows. Collection
  and artist totals emphasize albums, with track counts below, reusing summaries.
- Known original file formats, such as **FLAC and MP3**, appear below track
  durations on album pages, track search and Favourites. No extra requests are
  needed; these labels do not describe the stream's bitrate or resolution.

## Library and launcher improvements

- Disc grouping now also compares album year and the set of active-track upload
  dates. Different years or dates keep albums separate. This is display grouping,
  not a release identifier, and does not split uploads already inside one
  iBroadcast album.
- Duplicate candidates require the same positive track number and title within
  one disc. Repeated titles at different positions are no longer marked as
  duplicates. Audio and recording quality are not compared; trash still requires
  review and never deletes permanently.
- The desktop launcher remembers **Open browser automatically**, enabled by
  default. Untick it for wrappers such as Unite Pro; the manual browser button
  remains available. Closing the launcher stops only a server it started.
- Clearer **Apple Music / iTunes** source labels and quieter handling of browser
  requests that close before the server responds.
- The README includes current installation instructions, cleanup guidance and
  new screenshots showing these features.

## Downloads and updating

- **macOS Apple Silicon:** `tagcast-0.30.0-macos-arm64.zip`.
- **macOS Intel:** `tagcast-0.30.0-macos-x64.zip`.
- **Windows x64:** `tagcast-0.30.0-windows-x64.zip`.
- **Linux x64:** `tagcast-0.30.0-linux-x64.tar.gz`.

Each archive bundles Python, dependencies, a desktop launcher, a separate CLI
and license notices, with a companion SHA-256 checksum. Extract the whole package;
move `Tagcast.app` to Applications on macOS, open `Tagcast.exe` on Windows, or run
`./Tagcast` inside the extracted Linux folder.

**Stop the old Tagcast before starting 0.30.0**, and let any cleanup finish or stop
it first. Otherwise the new launcher opens the already-running server. Your
settings, tokens and cache stay in `~/.tagcast/`, or your configured `TAGCAST_HOME`.
Source installations remain supported with Python 3.11+ or uv.

See the [README](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/blob/v0.30.0/README.md)
and [cleanup guide](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/blob/v0.30.0/docs/metadata-cleanup.md)
for the complete steps. Your local music files are never changed. Playback does
not report plays or Last.fm scrobbles; the queue remains in this browser session.
